judge_response:
ANALYSIS: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is a functional gastrointestinal disorder diagnosed based on symptom criteria (e.g., Rome IV), characterized by recurrent abdominal pain associated with altered bowel habits. It is clinically subclassified into subtypes: IBS-D (diarrhea-predominant), IBS-C (constipation-predominant), IBS-M (mixed), and IBS-U (unsubtyped), based on stool consistency (Bristol Stool Form Scale) and symptom patterns.

The reference diagnosis is the broad category “Irritable Bowel Syndrome”; the predicted diagnosis specifies “Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), diarrhea-predominant (IBS-D)”. This is a more precise, clinically informative diagnosis — consistent with and fully contained within the reference diagnosis — provided the patient’s symptoms align (e.g., >25% of stools are loose/watery, <25% are hard/lumpy). Subtyping guides management (e.g., loperamide or eluxadoline for IBS-D vs. laxatives for IBS-C) and is standard in clinical practice and guidelines.

No overinterpretation or contradiction is present; the prediction enhances diagnostic specificity without exceeding evidence.

VERDICT: CORRECT
